authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Controller - Formal Execution.md, §II (Stability — Lyapunov's condition), §IV (Supervisory control — Sheridan's automation levels), §VII (Governance signal quality — Shannon's SNR), and the Controller Additions (the potential well W(s) = d(s,V))
note: SPEC vectors for the Controller's governance decision-math, and for the loop closing through a human. Authored from the article, not generated from the reference engine.

divergence.statement: The article's own Sustena Note says it plainly: 'the current code ships neither the table nor the four functions'. Re-confirmed by grep — should_surface, is_stable_intervention, compute_urgency, AUTOMATION_LEVEL, sheridan and lyapunov are all grep-0 in apps/api/sustena/.

term_by_term.is_stable_intervention (§II): RUST-AHEAD. There is no notion of a good decision anywhere in the reference — an approved proposal executes because it was approved, not because it was shown to reduce anything. Nothing computes a distance before and after.
term_by_term.AUTOMATION_LEVEL (§IV): RUST-AHEAD. No Sheridan table exists, so there is no declared 'how much does the human decide' dial. Which actions need approval is implicit in which code paths happen to route through the Council.
term_by_term.should_surface / SNR (§VII): RUST-AHEAD. Nothing filters what reaches a person on governance grounds. The Curated UI's knapsack limits HOW MANY widgets are shown, which is a different question from whether an event warrants a human decision at all.
term_by_term.urgency as Lyapunov-derived (§VII): RUST-AHEAD, and now possible for the first time: it needs W = d(s,V), which region.rs shipped in the previous slice. The reference's urgency is pct = spent/allocated, which is not derived from a stability condition and cannot be.

divergence.what_python_does_have_and_why_it_is_not_: The reference has real, working execute + rollback + council: control.execute_approved runs a PASSED proposal and control.rollback restores a prior snapshot, and the CouncilSession genuinely deliberates. That is the MECHANISM of human-in-the-loop governance, and it is not nothing. What is missing is the DECISION-MATH around it — nothing decides whether an intervention is a good one, nothing decides whether it is worth interrupting someone about, and nothing declares which action types need asking at all.
divergence.one_deliberate_departure_from_the_articl: §II writes the Lyapunov function as V(s) = ‖s_desired − s_actual‖² — distance to a POINT. The Controller's own Additions correct this to the potential well W(s) = d(s,V), and that is what is implemented: the viable region IS the desired set. A point target would need a desired point nobody declared and would make every state but one 'bad'. Using the region also means the Controller, the Monitor and the Curated UI all consume ONE quantity, which is the property the whole design rests on.
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged; nothing in them is Rust-specific.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. The Controller is a new additive module and touches no existing gate path.

stability_cases.name: an_intervention_that_reduces_the_distance_is_stable
stability_cases.why: §II's formal definition of a good decision: an intervention is valid IF AND ONLY IF it reduces the Lyapunov distance. −300 → −100 is 200 closer to the region.

stability_cases.name: an_intervention_that_increases_the_distance_is_not
stability_cases.why: And the rollback panel's purpose follows immediately: an action that increased W moved away from the region, so the previous state was closer.

stability_cases.name: holding_still_is_stable_because_the_condition_is_non_strict
stability_cases.why: W(after) ≤ W(before), not <. Doing nothing does not move away, and demanding strict improvement would forbid every holding action.

stability_cases.name: reaching_the_region_is_the_strongest_stable_move
stability_cases.why: Inside V, W = 0 — the potential well's floor.

stability_cases.name: a_comparison_against_a_lower_bound_is_reported_not_trusted
stability_cases.why: A violated cross-dimension relation makes the box distance a lower bound, so ordering two such numbers is not reliable. Reporting that beats a confident wrong answer about whether a decision was good.

sheridan_cases.name: the_approval_line_is_level_five
sheridan_cases.why: §IV: Sustena's Controller operates at levels 5–6, and `level ≤ 5` is §VII's condition. 5 executes if the human approves; 6 executes and notifies.

sheridan_cases.name: the_articles_table_routes_as_it_says
sheridan_cases.why: The article's own AUTOMATION_LEVEL, reproduced: ROUTINE executes and notifies; FINANCIAL, CRITICAL, IOT_WRITE and ROLLBACK all require approval.

sheridan_cases.name: an_undeclared_action_type_surfaces_rather_than_automating_itself
sheridan_cases.why: Fail-safe defaults at the governance layer. Forgetting a declaration must not be how something starts running unattended — so an unknown action type routes to ExecuteIfApproved, and is also reported as undeclared.

urgency_cases.name: urgency_rises_with_distance_from_the_region
urgency_cases.why: THE point of §VII: the urgency function is itself Lyapunov-derived. Events that move the system further from its viable region score higher, and that is not heuristic — it follows directly from the stability condition.

urgency_cases.name: a_state_inside_the_region_has_zero_urgency
urgency_cases.why: W = 0 inside V, so nothing is pulling. The Controller has nothing to escalate about a household that is fine.

urgency_cases.name: the_declared_base_weight_scales_it
urgency_cases.why: URGENCY_WEIGHTS is a spec field — the same discipline as the region weights and the CUSUM parameters. Same distance, two declared weights, two answers.

urgency_cases.name: a_nearer_deadline_raises_the_pressure
urgency_cases.why: time_pressure = 1/(deadline − now). The third factor of the §VII product.

urgency_cases.name: no_deadline_means_no_time_pressure_not_zero_urgency
urgency_cases.why: The article's own fallback: `1.0` when there is no deadline. Zero would silently suppress every open-ended event.

urgency_cases.name: a_passed_deadline_is_refused_rather_than_clamped
urgency_cases.why: 1/(deadline − now) with a passed deadline divides by zero or goes negative, which would silently INVERT the ranking. 'This was due yesterday' is a real condition the host should handle, not a number to invent.

urgency_cases.name: an_inexact_lyapunov_term_is_flagged_on_the_urgency
urgency_cases.why: When W is only a lower bound, the urgency is an UNDER-estimate — and an under-estimate must not quietly rank low.

routing_cases.name: an_urgent_action_needing_approval_surfaces
routing_cases.why: φ(e) = 1 ⟺ level ≤ 5 ∧ urgency ≥ θ. Both hold.

routing_cases.name: an_automated_action_goes_to_the_monitor_not_the_human
routing_cases.why: Above the approval line the human is not part of this loop — HOWEVER urgent. That is what the Sheridan level means, and the urgency term does not override it.

routing_cases.name: withholding_is_not_automating
routing_cases.why: THE MOST IMPORTANT DISTINCTION IN THE MODULE. An action that needs approval but is too quiet to interrupt does NOT proceed — nobody is being asked about it yet, and that is all. Folding 'not surfaced' into 'automated' would turn an attention filter into an auto-approver, which is the one way this design could fail dangerously.

routing_cases.name: the_declared_threshold_moves_the_line
routing_cases.why: θ_user is a declared preference — how much noise this person will accept. Same event, two tolerances, two answers.

routing_cases.name: a_surfaced_decision_carries_the_stability_verdict_when_one_can_be_made
routing_cases.why: The Controller filters AND validates. With a candidate after-state it can vouch that the intervention reduces W.

routing_cases.name: an_unassessed_intervention_is_not_vouched_for
routing_cases.why: 'Not assessed' and 'assessed and unstable' are different states, and neither is a yes. With no candidate after-state the Controller still surfaces — it just does not vouch.

routing_cases.name: an_unstable_intervention_still_surfaces_but_is_not_vouched_for
routing_cases.why: The Controller does not hide a bad idea from the person — it shows it and says it is a bad idea. Filtering is about ATTENTION, not truth.

declaration_cases.name: the_preferences_are_checked_at_authoring_time
declaration_cases.why: A negative θ or a negative weight silently inverts the filter.

declaration_cases.name: a_missing_urgency_weight_does_not_make_something_invisible
declaration_cases.why: Defaulting to 0.0 would silently suppress every unweighted event — a governance filter must not fail closed on ATTENTION. The fallback is 1.0, so an undeclared weight leaves urgency equal to the Lyapunov term.

loop_case.name: monitor_to_controller_to_human_to_gate_end_to_end
loop_case.why: THE SLICE'S POINT: the loop closes through a human, using only pieces earlier slices built. The Monitor's CUSUM sees a sustained distance from V; the Controller filters it past the SNR threshold and validates it against the Lyapunov condition; the decision surfaces with the binding a token must match; a HUMAN approving is the only step that mints one; the gate then admits exactly that act. And the same approval cannot be spent twice.
